text.p: Goodman Fielder Ltd chairman David Clarke said on Wednesday the food company is comfortable with analysts' profit estimates for the group in the year to June 30, 1997.
"I think the range is between A$114 million and A$119 million. We are comfortable with that," Clarke told reporters after speaking to the Australian Institute of Company Directors.
Goodman Fielder, Australasia's largest food group, reported a 1995/96 net profit of A$28.3 million, after taking an after-tax abnormal charge of A$72 million.
The company, which has improved its performance under chief executive David Hearn, has previously forecast it would achieve double-digit earnings growth for the 1996/97 year.
The bulk of the improvement was expected to come in the second half because of lower wheat costs.
Goodman recorded a first half net profit of A$55.8 million, versus A$45.9 million a year earlier.
Goodman Fielder is due to report its annual results on September 5.
